title: The login helper reads its credential record from a descriptor the client names, and the caller wired that descriptor to the client
index_line: T-0080 · AUTH_DECISION · SSH rekey skips auth, then username '-2' makes the login helper read the trusted record from the client's terminal · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: The login helper assumed its argv came from a trusted local parent: a user name of '-2' is an instruction meaning 'read the credential record from descriptor 2'. The SSH service connected that descriptor to the client's session terminal, so an unauthenticated client supplied the record the helper treated as a trusted local statement of identity and policy.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated SSH client requests a rekey; completing it moves the connection into the connection-protocol phase although no user has authenticated
the phase transition is not gated on the session having an assigned policy, so the client opens a session channel and sends an exec request
the SSH service spawns RouterOS's login helper with the client-supplied user name as a command-line argument
the helper interprets a leading '-' as control syntax; '-2' selects descriptor 2 as the source of the trusted login record instead of its normal local input
descriptor 2 on the helper is the client's session terminal, so the attacker writes the record the helper believes came from a trusted local process
the helper installs the attacker-named identity and the supplied policy mask, yielding an administrative session without a password or key

source.protocol.value: the SSH transport: a rekey request from an unauthenticated client, then a session channel whose user name is attacker-chosen

guard.session-state.value: the connection-protocol dispatcher's failure to require an assigned policy before dispatching connection-layer requests

sink.exec.noshell.value: the login helper is exec'd with the user name as an argv element; a leading dash turns data into an instruction (descriptor selector)

encoding.shell.value: the '-N' token is an argument encoding the helper interprets, not a literal user name

preconditions.expr: the SSH service is reachable and accepts a session channel

check.spec: timeout 8 ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o PreferredAuthentications=none -o ConnectTimeout=5 HOST exit 2>&1 | head -3

preconditions.expr: the build predates 7.23.4 (dispatcher policy check) or 7.23.4+ (login-helper argv hardening) as applicable

check.spec: timeout 8 ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no HOST 2>&1 | head -2; printf 'check RouterOS version via SNMP/API or /system/resource/print\n'

preconditions.expr: the login helper is reachable with an attacker-chosen argv from an unauthenticated connection

success: a session channel opens and an exec request is dispatched before any authentication
the console reports the administrator identity and the full policy mask although no credential was presented
failure_like: the dispatcher refuses connection-layer requests until a policy is assigned (patched 7.23.4)
the login helper rejects user names beginning with '-' or containing control bytes
false_positive: an SSH banner or a pre-auth 'none' auth failure is not the bypass — require a session channel plus an exec that the device executed
a read-only prompt is not administrative identity; compare the policy mask against a known full set

hazards: any service that passes an untrusted principal name as argv to a privileged helper
helpers that accept '-N' as 'read my credentials from descriptor N' (a legacy local-IPC idiom)
stage one needs only a protocol phase-transition bug — rekey, STARTTLS, or any renegotiation that re-enters the state machine
non_transfers: helpers that take the principal on stdin or via a fixed structure with an explicit length
protocol stacks that bind the phase transition to an authenticated session object

evidence.target: MikroTik RouterOS 7.x (and 6.x for stage one), SSH service + login helper (CVE-2026-67279, 'MikroTrick')

provenance.author: Bishop Fox (MikroTrick research)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-67279 chain: completing a client-requested SSH rekey moves the connection into the connection-protocol phase with no authenticated identity; the login helper is then spawned with the client username as argv, a username of -2 selects descriptor 2 as the trusted login record, and that descriptor is the client terminal — full policy mask installed without authentication

provenance.author: CERT Polska (Slawomir Rozbicki)
provenance.corroborates: independent discovery and coordination: CVE-2026-67279 — RouterOS SSH enters the connection protocol after a client-requested rekey even though user authentication was never attempted, allowing an unauthenticated client to open a session channel and send an exec request
